I will keep it simple and do what fits my place in Quzhou County best: I will plant a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on all my land. That is the most steady way for me to earn, and it matches our fields, water conditions, and the work rhythm I know well. I do not want to spread myself across many crops, because that raises labor, management difficulty, and risk. I will use improved winter wheat seed and hybrid summer maize seed, put most of my attention on base fertilizer, watering at the key stages, and a few timely pesticide sprays instead of chasing very high input. For wheat, I will focus on strong seedlings, overwintering, spring water, and disease control around the jointing and heading stages. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow maize, keep the stubble and use lighter tillage to save time and moisture, then manage fertilizer and water around the big-flare and grain-filling stages. My goal is stable yield, not gambling on a fancy crop.
